A_open.text: Monday morning. Brad has been up since six. He now has strong opinions about pumpkins.
I hauled forty pumpkins before breakfast. I can't feel my arms.
That's the farm lifestyle. Welcome. Coffee?
Jane hands over a coffee and a campus map. The map is marked up in three colors of pen.
Dad made me your orientation buddy. Don't look so thrilled.
I'm thrilled. I'm just also asleep.

then.text: How's your pride after Doris? Still in the haystack?
I'm told there's still some in my hair.

else.text: Doris says hi. She thinks you're a good pusher.

A_open.text: Freshmen! Gather round! Name tags, please! We lose one student a year to anonymity!
A tour guide pins a name tag on Brad's shirt. It reads: BRAD BART (LEGACY!)
It means your dad's name is on a plaque somewhere. A plaque nobody reads.
On your left, the Founder's Fountain! Built in 1887 by a man who really loved fountains.
He founded it by falling in.
I've done this tour three times. Want my shortcut? Or you can stay for the fountain facts.

A_open.prompt: Jane is already looking at a gap in the hedge.

do.text: Lead the way.
Behind a hedge, through a gate, up a spiral stair. The bell tower, quiet and empty.
Everyone thinks it's locked. It isn't. It's just shy.
The whole valley is spread below. The college, the town, and a far corner of orange fields.
That's our farm. See the little barn? I used to come up here to find it.
It looks peaceful from up here.
It's peaceful from everywhere. That's the problem. Don't tell anyone about this spot.
Your secret's safe with me.
A crow lands on the tower bell. It looks at Brad. Then at Jane. Then at the secret.
...Fine. Brad, the crow. The crow, Brad. We're all in this together.
I'll stay. I should learn the fountain facts.
Brave. Stay and heckle with me.
Everyone gets an Orientation Bingo card! Fill a row, win a tote bag!
Nobody's ever gotten bingo. I think the tote bag is a myth.
Challenge accepted.
I like you. You're an optimist. It's like watching a puppy try stairs.

A_open.text: I have to check in with the TA office. You've got a Bingo card. Pick your stops.
There's time for two before the welcome speech. Lecture hall at noon. Don't be late.

B_quad.text: Orientation Bingo: walk to a door and press Action. You have time for two stops.

on_max.text: The campus bell strikes noon. The welcome speech is starting.

do.text: Bingo square: FOUNDER'S FOUNTAIN. Someone has tossed a pumpkin seed in. Again.
Why are there pumpkin seeds in every fountain?
Bingo square: BOOKSTORE. A sign reads: TEXTBOOKS SOLD OUT. ASK ABOUT RAVEN STICKERS.
I'll take the raven sticker. It seems like the college's whole personality.

stop_s.text: The library is hushed and enormous. Somewhere, a stack of books has been left looking guilty.
Icebreaker time! Find someone who has a pet! Find someone who has FEELINGS!
A hand shoots out from between two shelves and drags Brad into the stacks.

then.text: Porch boy. Quiet. Sit.
Closed to optimism. Good to see you again.

else.text: Sandra Stump. My family owns the Log and Stump. Now sit.

stop_s.text: Anyone back there? Anyone who wants a free lanyard?
I'm hiding from the icebreaker. I'm not good at feelings in groups.
Why are you teaching me how to hide?
You're a witness now. A test. Question one: when is quiet hour in this library?
Wrong. Whichever hour Mrs. Alder is awake for. Question two: how many crows on the college crest?
Is someone in the stacks? Hello?

stop_s.prompt: The icebreaker leader is getting close.

do.text: Nobody here but us books.
Hm. Sounds like a book. Carry on.
...You lied for me. Strangers don't usually do that.
We're not strangers. We took a trivia test.
She's over here!
Found you! You've won the Honest Citizen Award! Here's a ribbon!
Brad is handed a ribbon that reads: HONEST CITIZEN. Sandra is handed a lanyard.
Nice. Very noble. I'll remember this.
I'm very sorry. I panicked.

stop_s.text: You're the Bart kid. Staying at McVine's. News travels. The tavern has ears.
You made Gord smile at dinner. Nobody's done that since 1998.
Intro Bio, Section B. I checked the roster. We're lab partners.

stop_g.text: In the student centre, a coffee cart has a line. Behind it, a blonde girl is on her own.

then.text: Brad! You came back! I'm covering the welcome cart. Dale called in sick.
He ate one of my muffins. He's fine. He's been fine for two days. In bed.

else.text: Oh! A new face! I know all the faces. Can you take orders? Dale called in sick.
I'm Georgia, Grove Cafe. He ate one of my muffins. He's fine. In bed. For two days.

stop_g.text: Hi, I'm Brad. Sure, I can take orders.

then.text: Any feelings since the cookie? Just curious.
Why would I have feelings?
No reason! Cart! Orders! Go!

stop_g.text: For ten minutes Brad takes orders, steams milk, and learns the cart has a mind of its own.
Don't mind Gertrude. She hisses when she likes you.
Everything has a name. Even the muffin. Please, taste-test it.
The muffin is orange. It smells of cinnamon and a faint hint of the sea.
It's pumpkin, cinnamon, and a little anchovy. Be honest.

stop_g.prompt: Georgia watches, hopeful, as Brad takes a bite.

do.text: It's... weird. But I want a second bite. Why do I want a second bite?
That's the best review I've ever gotten! Weird but wanting more!
Everyone else just says 'It's great.' You told me the truth.
It's delicious! Really!
You blinked three times. I saw it.
Okay, it's a lot. But I admire the courage.
I'll take courage! Thanks for being kind.

stop_g.text: You're good at this. Come by the cafe sometime. Free coffee for cart staff.
Also, fair warning. Professor Peters's speeches are legendary. Last year the sprinklers went off.

stop_p.text: The lecture hall is empty except for one professor and one very large projector.
You are not a projector. You are a box. A box that listens.
Display. DISPLAY. I am the professor. I outrank you.
The projector blinks. It smells faintly of toast.
Take a seat. Row one. Not near the projector. It knows.

then.text: Mr. Bart. We met at the gate. We do not speak of the gate.
What gate?
Exactly.

else.text: I don't believe we've met. Patricia Peters, Biology. And you are?

then.text: Her eyes drop to Brad's boots. They linger.
Those boots look familiar.

p_bart.text: Any relation to a Daniel Bart? He attended Ravenwood. Years ago.

do.text: Yes. He's my dad. He told me a lot of stories about this place.
I'm sure he did. He was... memorable.
Be careful which of those stories you believe.
Bart's a pretty common name.
Is it? I've never met another one.
No matter. You may keep your secrets, Mr. Bart. I certainly keep mine.

D_speech.text: The lecture hall fills with freshmen, name tags, and the smell of nervous coffee.
Brad! Over here! I saved you a seat. Sort of. I put my bag on it.

then.text: Is this seat taken? Oh! New face! I know all the faces. I'm Georgia.
Brad. Nice to meet you.

else.text: Georgia slides in beside Jane, carrying two lattes. She waves with her elbow.

then.text: You're in my row. Sandra Stump. Don't talk to me.
I'm Brad. I didn't know it was your row.
All rows are my row if I'm in them.

else.text: Sandra sits at the back, slouched, hood up. She raises two fingers. It might be a wave.

then.text: At the podium, Patricia glances at the seats and spots Brad.

D_speech.text: Welcome to Ravenwood College. Founded 1887. Home to scholarship and many, many crows.
First slide, please.
The screen shows a picture of a raven. Upside down.
That is not the right slide. That is... a raven. Next slide.
The projector hums. Then it sputters. Then, a small orange flame appears.
It's tradition! I told you!
Nobody panic. This is a controlled... Oh, it's on fire.

D_speech.prompt: The projector is on fire. Everyone is looking at Brad.

do.text: I've got it!
Brad sprints down the aisle and rips the extinguisher off the wall.
Sorry, Georgia!
That was a seasonal blend!
The flames grow. Coffee, it turns out, is only a suggestion. Brad grabs the extinguisher.
FIRE!
Thank you. We hadn't noticed.
Embarrassed, Brad snatches the extinguisher off the wall.

D_speech.text: A cloud of foam fills the hall. When it clears, the fire is out and Brad is white head to toe.
Remarkable. A raven did it.
A raven started the fire?
Obviously. There's one in the window.
The crow looks at Brad. It leans in, plucks his name tag from his shirt, and flies out the window.
Hey! That was my name tag!
It reads BRAD BART (LEGACY!). It is gone.
Best orientation ever! I'm going to remember this when I'm eighty!
Not bad. For a hero.
I'm going to put this on a cake!
Mr. Bart. You will assist in my lab on Wednesday. As a reward.
That's a reward?
It's a reward with chemicals. Class dismissed. Nobody mention the fire in the evaluations.
My name tag said LEGACY. Somewhere out there, a crow knows my business.
